title: 20 lines of code that will beat A/B testing every time
summary: The epsilon-greedy multi-armed bandit algorithm provides a superior alternative to A/B testing by automatically exploring different options 10% of the time while exploiting the best-performing choice 90% of the time, requiring only simple code changes to implement continuous optimization.
when-to-read: Read this article when you need to optimize between multiple choices (button colors, copy, designs) and want a method that continuously adapts without manual intervention. If you're specifically designing statistical experiments to measure causal effects with rigorous controls, consult A/B testing methodologies instead, as this article's epsilon-greedy approach trades some statistical purity for practical optimization.
